To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the employment of single black mothers with young children is associated with their higher self efficacy beliefs, which in turn is associated with less depression, which in turn leads to more frequent contact with their nonresident partners and better parenting in the home.
the influence of mothers low wage employment on children's development is largely indirect and mediated through mothers' self efficacy and parenting.
employment is indirectly related to the development of young children through the mediating effects of maternal self efficacy, maternal depression, and maternal parenting in the home.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions What are the relations between employment, self efficacy beliefs, and parenting in the context of single black mother families How do employment, self efficacy, parenting, and the mother nonresident relationship interact in the development of children's cognitive and social emotional functioning in the early years of school attendance How does employment, self efficacy and parenting in the preschool years relate to the development of children s cognitive and social emotional skills in early elementary school What is the mediating role of parenting in the home in the relation
how the economic and social context in which single black mothers and children live affects their psychological well being, parenting behaviors, and children's development.
the role of maternal self efficacy and parenting in the link between employment, income, and children's development among low income single black mothers and children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of low income employment on the psychological well being, parenting, and child development of single black mothers and preschoolers are not yet known.

there is little conclusive evidence that welfare reform has improved the well being of single mothers and their young families, and that the evidence is mixed as to whether welfare reform has improved children's development (Grogger Karoly, 2005; Grogger Karoly Seefeldt, 2002)

the relationship between employment and parenting and child development is mediated by maternal self efficacy, and that employment is related to maternal self efficacy through the mediating role of maternal depressive symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of low income employment and low wage employment in single parent families are mediated by maternal self efficacy and the quality of the maternal nonresident father relationship (see Jackson Huang, 1999 2000; Huang, Jackson, 1999a, 1999b)
the quality of the relationship between the mother and nonresident father influences the frequency of nonresidential father's contacts with his child (Amato, 1993; Furstenberg Morgan, 1994)

nonresident fathers' involvement with their children is related to better child outcomes (Amato, 1998; Amato Gilbreth 1999; Amato Gilrain, 1999a, 1999b; Furstenberg, Nord, Peterson, 1987; Lamb, Pleck, Charnov, Levine, 1985; Seltzer 1991; Seltzer Bianchi, 1988; Seltzer Lloyd, 2001).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of single black mothers' parenting in the home is related to their employment, perceived self efficacy, depressive symptoms, the quality of their relationships with nonresident black fathers, the frequency of nonresidential fathers' visits, and the children's subsequent development in early elementary school The findings are discussed in the light of social cognitive theory (Bandura,1997, 1999).

low wage employment, which has become a requirement for single mothers receiving public assistance, is not necessarily the panacea for the well being and development of children that it has been made out to be.

the effects of low wage employment among low income single black mothers on children's development are mediated by maternal self efficacy, maternal depressive symptoms, and the quality of maternal nonresident father relationships.
